# Sex-resolved protein abundance summaries

The composition-level 3 × 2 analysis above already evaluates Treatment, Sex, and Treatment × Sex for cellular-component fractions. The sections below add the protein-level sex-resolved summaries used in the Adult-vs-Old composition workflow.

For each retained protein, mean and median abundance are calculated among **positive detections only** within each Treatment × Sex group. Detection counts and prevalence are exported alongside abundance so that low-detection proteins can be interpreted appropriately.

```{r sex-resolved-abundance-summary}
abundance_by_trt_sex <- long_filt %>%
  group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Treatment, Sex) %>%
  summarise(
    detected_n = sum(Intensity > 0, na.rm = TRUE),

    total_n = n(),

    prevalence = detected_n /
      total_n,

    mean_intensity = if (any(Intensity > 0, na.rm = TRUE)) {
      mean(Intensity[Intensity > 0], na.rm = TRUE)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },

    median_intensity = if (any(Intensity > 0, na.rm = TRUE)) {
      median(Intensity[Intensity > 0], na.rm = TRUE)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    },

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Treatment = factor(Treatment, levels = c("Control", "Exercise", "Rapamycin")),

    Sex = factor(Sex, levels = c("Female", "Male")),

    Group = factor(
      paste(Treatment, Sex, sep = "_"),
      levels = c(
        "Control_Female",
        "Exercise_Female",
        "Rapamycin_Female",
        "Control_Male",
        "Exercise_Male",
        "Rapamycin_Male"
      )
    )
  )

write.csv(
  abundance_by_trt_sex,
  file.path(split_dot_dir, "Protein_abundance_by_Treatment_Sex.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

abundance_by_trt_sex_wide <- abundance_by_trt_sex %>%
  select(
    Protein.Group,
    Gene1,
    Bin,
    Treatment,
    Sex,
    detected_n,
    total_n,
    prevalence,
    mean_intensity,
    median_intensity
  ) %>%
  mutate(Group = paste(Treatment, Sex, sep = "_")) %>%
  select(-Treatment, -Sex) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Group,
    values_from = c(detected_n, total_n, prevalence, mean_intensity, median_intensity)
  )

write.csv(
  abundance_by_trt_sex_wide,
  file.path(split_dot_dir, "Protein_abundance_by_Treatment_Sex_wide.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# Sex-specific Top-10 rankings

The pooled-Control display above holds the protein set constant across sexes. The analyses below answer a different question: **which proteins are most abundant within Old-Control Female and Old-Control Male mice separately?**

Within each sex, the Top-10 list is ranked by Old-Control abundance, and the same proteins are then shown in Control, Exercise, and Rapamycin mice of that sex.

```{r sex-specific-top10-functions}
make_sex_specific_top10 <- function(sex_name) {

  ranking <- abundance_by_trt_sex %>%
    filter(
      as.character(Sex) ==
        sex_name,
      as.character(Treatment) ==
        "Control",
      Bin %in%
        dot_bin_order,
      !is.na(mean_intensity),
      mean_intensity > 0
    ) %>%
    group_by(Bin) %>%
    arrange(desc(mean_intensity), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    slice_head(n = 10) %>%
    mutate(Rank_Control = row_number()) %>%
    ungroup()

  display_data <- ranking %>%
    select(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Rank_Control) %>%
    inner_join(
      abundance_by_trt_sex %>%
        filter(as.character(Sex) == sex_name) %>%
        select(
          Protein.Group,
          Gene1,
          Bin,
          Treatment,
          mean_intensity,
          median_intensity,
          detected_n,
          total_n,
          prevalence
        ),
      by = c("Protein.Group", "Gene1", "Bin")
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Treatment = factor(Treatment, levels = c("Control", "Exercise", "Rapamycin")),

      log10_intensity = if_else(!is.na(mean_intensity) & mean_intensity > 0, log10(mean_intensity), NA_real_)
    )

  log_vals <- display_data$log10_intensity
  log_vals <- log_vals[is.finite(log_vals)]

  size_lims <- c(floor(min(log_vals, na.rm = TRUE)), ceiling(max(log_vals, na.rm = TRUE)))

  size_brks <- pretty(range(log_vals, na.rm = TRUE), n = 4)

  size_brks <- size_brks[size_brks >= size_lims[1] & size_brks <= size_lims[2]]

  panel_list <- list()

  for (i in seq_along(dot_bin_order)) {

    bin_name <- dot_bin_order[i]

    rank_bin <- ranking %>%
      filter(Bin == bin_name) %>%
      arrange(Rank_Control) %>%
      mutate(GeneLabel = make.unique(as.character(Gene1)))

    plot_df <- display_data %>%
      filter(Bin == bin_name) %>%
      left_join(rank_bin %>% select(Protein.Group, GeneLabel), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
      mutate(GeneLabel = factor(GeneLabel, levels = rev(rank_bin$GeneLabel)))

    if (nrow(plot_df) == 0) {
      next
    }

    bin_col <- bin_pal_dot[[bin_name]]

    panel_list[[bin_name]] <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Treatment, y = GeneLabel, size = log10_intensity)) +

      geom_point(colour = bin_col, alpha = 0.90, na.rm = TRUE, show.legend = i == 1) +

      scale_size_continuous(
        name = expression(log[10]("mean intensity")),
        range = c(nm_style$top10_bubble_min, nm_style$top10_bubble_max),
        limits =
          size_lims,
        breaks =
          size_brks
      ) +

      scale_x_discrete(position = "top", labels = c("Control" = "Ctl", "Exercise" = "Ex", "Rapamycin" = "Rapa")) +

      guides(size = guide_legend(override.aes = list(colour = "grey35", alpha = 1))) +

      labs(title = bin_name, x = NULL, y = NULL) +

      theme_classic(base_size = 11) +

      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = nm_style$component_heading, colour = bin_col),

        axis.text.x.top = element_text(size = nm_style$top10_group_pt, face = "bold"),

        axis.text.y = element_text(size = nm_style$top10_protein_pt),

        axis.line = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),

        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "grey93", linewidth = nm_style$bubble_grid_line),

        panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey93", linewidth = nm_style$bubble_grid_line),

        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
      )
  }

  combined_plot <-
    patchwork::wrap_plots(panel_list, ncol = 4) +

    patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") +

    patchwork::plot_annotation() &

    theme(legend.position = "right")

  list(ranking = ranking, display_data = display_data, plot = combined_plot)
}
```

# Female-versus-Male Top-10 membership overlap

This comparison asks whether the proteins that dominate each cellular component in Old-Control muscle are the same in Female and Male mice.

```{r top10-sex-membership-overlap}
female_membership <- female_top10$ranking %>%
  transmute(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Female_rank = Rank_Control, Female_Top10 = TRUE)

male_membership <- male_top10$ranking %>%
  transmute(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Male_rank = Rank_Control, Male_Top10 = TRUE)

top10_sex_overlap <- full_join(female_membership, male_membership, by = c("Protein.Group", "Gene1", "Bin")) %>%
  mutate(
    Female_Top10 = replace_na(Female_Top10, FALSE),

    Male_Top10 = replace_na(Male_Top10, FALSE),

    Membership = case_when(
      Female_Top10 &
        Male_Top10 ~
        "Both sexes",

      Female_Top10 &
        !Male_Top10 ~
        "Female only",

      !Female_Top10 &
        Male_Top10 ~
        "Male only",

      TRUE ~
        "Neither"
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    factor(Bin, levels = dot_bin_order),
    factor(Membership, levels = c("Both sexes", "Female only", "Male only")),
    Female_rank,
    Male_rank
  )

top10_overlap_summary <- top10_sex_overlap %>%
  filter(Membership != "Neither") %>%
  count(Bin, Membership, name = "n") %>%
  tidyr::complete(
    Bin =
      dot_bin_order,
    Membership = c("Both sexes", "Female only", "Male only"),
    fill = list(n = 0)
  )

write.csv(
  top10_sex_overlap,
  file.path(split_dot_dir, "Top10_Female_Male_membership_overlap.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  top10_overlap_summary,
  file.path(split_dot_dir, "Top10_Female_Male_membership_summary.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(top10_overlap_summary, caption = "Female-versus-Male overlap of Old-Control Top-10 proteins")
```

# Sex-specific detection-frequency analysis

Detection is now evaluated separately within Female and Male mice.

For each sex, two independent two-sided Fisher exact tests are performed:

- Old Control versus Old+Exercise
- Old Control versus Old+Rapamycin

BH-FDR correction is applied separately within each sex and treatment comparison, using the comparison-specific testable universe. A protein is testable when it is detected in at least two samples in **either** group of that comparison within the same sex.

The principal descriptive loss criterion is:

- **Treatment-reduced:** Control detected ≥2 and Treatment detected ≤1.

An exact-loss subset additionally requires Treatment detected =0.

```{r sex-specific-detection-analysis}
test_detection_pair <- function(control_det, control_total, treatment_det, treatment_total) {

  if (any(is.na(c(control_det, control_total, treatment_det, treatment_total)))) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  mat <- matrix(
    c(control_det, control_total - control_det, treatment_det, treatment_total - treatment_det),
    nrow = 2,
    byrow = TRUE
  )

  tryCatch(stats::fisher.test(mat)$p.value, error = function(e) NA_real_)
}

bh_on_testable <- function(p, testable) {

  out <- rep(NA_real_, length(p))

  idx <- which(testable & !is.na(p))

  if (length(idx) > 0) {
    out[idx] <- p.adjust(p[idx], method = "BH")
  }

  out
}

detection_bysex_counts <- long_assigned %>%
  mutate(Detected = Intensity > 0) %>%
  group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Sex, Treatment) %>%
  summarise(
    detected_n = sum(Detected, na.rm = TRUE),

    total_n = n(),

    prevalence =
      detected_n /
        total_n,

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Treatment, values_from = c(detected_n, total_n, prevalence), names_sep = "_")

detection_bysex <- detection_bysex_counts %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    p_Exercise = test_detection_pair(detected_n_Control, total_n_Control, detected_n_Exercise, total_n_Exercise),

    p_Rapamycin = test_detection_pair(detected_n_Control, total_n_Control, detected_n_Rapamycin, total_n_Rapamycin)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    Exercise_testable =
      detected_n_Control >=
        min_detect_n |
        detected_n_Exercise >=
          min_detect_n,

    Rapamycin_testable =
      detected_n_Control >=
        min_detect_n |
        detected_n_Rapamycin >=
          min_detect_n
  ) %>%
  group_by(Sex) %>%
  mutate(
    FDR_Exercise =
      bh_on_testable(p_Exercise, Exercise_testable),

    FDR_Rapamycin =
      bh_on_testable(p_Rapamycin, Rapamycin_testable)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    delta_prev_Exercise =
      prevalence_Exercise -
        prevalence_Control,

    delta_prev_Rapamycin =
      prevalence_Rapamycin -
        prevalence_Control,

    Exercise_exact_loss =
      detected_n_Control >=
        min_detect_n &
        detected_n_Exercise ==
          0,

    Rapamycin_exact_loss =
      detected_n_Control >=
        min_detect_n &
        detected_n_Rapamycin ==
          0,

    Exercise_reduced =
      detected_n_Control >=
        min_detect_n &
        detected_n_Exercise <=
          1,

    Rapamycin_reduced =
      detected_n_Control >=
        min_detect_n &
        detected_n_Rapamycin <=
          1,

    Exercise_gain =
      detected_n_Control <=
        1 &
        detected_n_Exercise >=
          min_detect_n,

    Rapamycin_gain =
      detected_n_Control <=
        1 &
        detected_n_Rapamycin >=
          min_detect_n,

    # ── Mutually exclusive relaxed loss-of-detection patterns ───────────────
    #
    # These reproduce the logic used in the pooled old-treatment detection
    # analysis, now within each sex.
    #
    # Shared loss:
    #   robust in Old Ctl, reduced/absent after BOTH interventions.
    #
    # Exercise-specific loss:
    #   robust in Old Ctl AND Old+Rapa, reduced/absent only after Exercise.
    #
    # Rapamycin-specific loss:
    #   robust in Old Ctl AND Old+Ex, reduced/absent only after Rapamycin.
    Shared_loss =
      detected_n_Control >=
        min_detect_n &
      detected_n_Exercise <=
        1 &
      detected_n_Rapamycin <=
        1,

    Exercise_specific_loss =
      detected_n_Control >=
        min_detect_n &
      detected_n_Exercise <=
        1 &
      detected_n_Rapamycin >=
        min_detect_n,

    Rapamycin_specific_loss =
      detected_n_Control >=
        min_detect_n &
      detected_n_Exercise >=
        min_detect_n &
      detected_n_Rapamycin <=
        1,

    Any_intervention_loss =
      Shared_loss |
        Exercise_specific_loss |
        Rapamycin_specific_loss,

    Detection_loss_pattern = case_when(
      Shared_loss ~
        "Shared loss",

      Exercise_specific_loss ~
        "Exercise-specific loss",

      Rapamycin_specific_loss ~
        "Rapamycin-specific loss",

      TRUE ~
        "None"
    )
  )

write.csv(detection_bysex, file.path(split_detect_dir, "Detection_bySex_all.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Sex-specific detection-loss patterns

The previous pairwise `Control versus Exercise` and `Control versus Rapamycin` flags are useful for statistical testing, but they do **not** define intervention specificity. For example, a protein can be reduced after Exercise and also reduced after Rapamycin.

To make the detection figures biologically interpretable, the plotted candidate sets are therefore divided into three **mutually exclusive relaxed patterns within each sex**:

1. **Shared loss:** Old Ctl ≥2, Old+Ex ≤1, and Old+Rapa ≤1.
2. **Exercise-specific loss:** Old Ctl ≥2, Old+Ex ≤1, and Old+Rapa ≥2.
3. **Rapamycin-specific loss:** Old Ctl ≥2, Old+Ex ≥2, and Old+Rapa ≤1.

Thus, an Exercise-specific candidate must remain robustly detected after Rapamycin, and a Rapamycin-specific candidate must remain robustly detected after Exercise.

The rightmost column displays the relevant **two-sided within-sex Fisher exact-test raw p-value**. BH-FDR values are retained in the exported tables.

```{r sex-specific-detection-pattern-plot-function}
format_detect_p <- function(p) {

  case_when(
    is.na(p) ~
      "p=NA",

    p <
      0.001 ~
      "p<0.001*",

    p <=
      0.05 ~
      paste0("p=", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3), "*"),

    TRUE ~
      paste0("p=", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3))
  )
}

make_sex_detection_pattern_plot <- function(pattern_name, sex_name, legend_bins, show_legend = TRUE) {

  pattern_name <- match.arg(pattern_name, c("Shared", "Exercise", "Rapamycin"))

  if (pattern_name == "Shared") {

    flag_col <-
      "Shared_loss"

    title_text <-
      sex_name

    subtitle_text <-
      paste0("Old Ctl ≥ ", min_detect_n, "; Old+Ex ≤ 1; Old+Rapa ≤ 1")

  } else if (pattern_name == "Exercise") {

    flag_col <-
      "Exercise_specific_loss"

    title_text <-
      sex_name

    subtitle_text <-
      paste0("Old Ctl ≥ ", min_detect_n, "; Old+Ex ≤ 1; Old+Rapa ≥ ", min_detect_n)

  } else {

    flag_col <-
      "Rapamycin_specific_loss"

    title_text <-
      sex_name

    subtitle_text <-
      paste0("Old Ctl ≥ ", min_detect_n, "; Old+Ex ≥ ", min_detect_n, "; Old+Rapa ≤ 1")
  }

  candidates <- detection_bysex %>%
    filter(as.character(Sex) == sex_name, .data[[flag_col]], Bin %in% dot_bin_order) %>%
    mutate(
      p_for_sort = case_when(
        pattern_name ==
          "Exercise" ~
          p_Exercise,

        pattern_name ==
          "Rapamycin" ~
          p_Rapamycin,

        TRUE ~
          pmin(p_Exercise, p_Rapamycin, na.rm = TRUE)
      )
    ) %>%
    arrange(factor(Bin, levels = dot_bin_order), p_for_sort, desc(detected_n_Control), Gene1)

  if (nrow(candidates) == 0) {

    return(
      ggplot() +

        annotate(
          "text",
          x = 0,
          y = 0,
          label =
            paste0("No ", tolower(pattern_name), " loss candidates"),
          size = 4
        ) +

        xlim(-1, 1) +

        ylim(-1, 1) +

        labs(title = title_text, subtitle = subtitle_text) +

        theme_void() +

        theme(
          plot.title =
            element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),

          plot.subtitle =
            element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 9.5)
        )
    )
  }

  candidates <- candidates %>%
    mutate(GeneLabel = make.unique(as.character(Gene1)), GeneLabel = factor(GeneLabel, levels = rev(GeneLabel)))

  candidate_long <- bind_rows(

    candidates %>%
      transmute(
        Protein.Group,
        Gene1,
        GeneLabel,
        Bin,
        Group =
          "Old Ctl",
        detected_n =
          detected_n_Control,
        total_n =
          total_n_Control
      ),

    candidates %>%
      transmute(
        Protein.Group,
        Gene1,
        GeneLabel,
        Bin,
        Group =
          "Old+Ex",
        detected_n =
          detected_n_Exercise,
        total_n =
          total_n_Exercise
      ),

    candidates %>%
      transmute(
        Protein.Group,
        Gene1,
        GeneLabel,
        Bin,
        Group =
          "Old+Rapa",
        detected_n =
          detected_n_Rapamycin,
        total_n =
          total_n_Rapamycin
      )
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      Group = factor(Group, levels = c("Old Ctl", "Old+Ex", "Old+Rapa")),

      state = case_when(detected_n >= min_detect_n ~ "robust", detected_n == 1 ~ "singleton", TRUE ~ "absent")
    )

    # Invisible points used only to generate one complete legend.
  # legend_bins contains only components represented in Female OR Male
  # for this specific detection pattern.
  legend_df <- tibble(
    Bin = factor(legend_bins, levels = legend_bins),

    Group = factor(rep("Old Ctl", length(legend_bins)), levels = c("Old Ctl", "Old+Ex", "Old+Rapa")),

    GeneLabel = factor(
      rep(levels(candidates$GeneLabel)[1], length(legend_bins)),
      levels =
        levels(candidates$GeneLabel)
    )
  )

  p_text <- candidates %>%
    mutate(
      p_label = case_when(
        pattern_name ==
          "Exercise" ~
          format_detect_p(p_Exercise),

        pattern_name ==
          "Rapamycin" ~
          format_detect_p(p_Rapamycin),

        TRUE ~
          paste0("Ex ", format_detect_p(p_Exercise), "\nRapa ", format_detect_p(p_Rapamycin))
      ),

      p_bold = case_when(
        pattern_name ==
          "Exercise" ~
          !is.na(p_Exercise) &
            p_Exercise <=
              0.05,

        pattern_name ==
          "Rapamycin" ~
          !is.na(p_Rapamycin) &
            p_Rapamycin <=
              0.05,

        TRUE ~
          (!is.na(p_Exercise) & p_Exercise <= 0.05) |
            (!is.na(p_Rapamycin) & p_Rapamycin <= 0.05)
      ),

      p_face = if_else(p_bold, "bold", "plain")
    )

  ggplot() +

    geom_segment(
      data = tibble(GeneLabel = levels(candidates$GeneLabel)),
      aes(x = 0.65, xend = 4.25, y = GeneLabel, yend = GeneLabel),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      colour = "grey93",
      linewidth = nm_style$detection_row_line
    ) +

    geom_point(
      data =
        candidate_long %>%
        filter(state == "absent"),
      aes(x = Group, y = GeneLabel),
      shape = 4,
      size = nm_style$detection_open,
      stroke = nm_style$detection_stroke,
      colour = "grey65"
    ) +

        geom_point(
      data =
        candidate_long %>%
        filter(state == "singleton"),
      aes(x = Group, y = GeneLabel, colour = Bin),
      shape = 1,
      size = nm_style$detection_open,
      stroke = nm_style$detection_stroke,
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +

        geom_point(
      data =
        candidate_long %>%
        filter(state == "robust"),
      aes(x = Group, y = GeneLabel, colour = Bin),
      shape = 16,
      size = nm_style$detection_filled,
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +

        geom_point(
      data =
        legend_df,

      aes(x = Group, y = GeneLabel, colour = Bin),

      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      shape = 16,
      size = nm_style$detection_filled,
      alpha = 0,

      show.legend =
        show_legend
    ) +

    # Show n/N only for robust (filled) dots.
    geom_text(
      data =
        candidate_long %>%
        filter(state == "robust"),
      aes(x = Group, y = GeneLabel, label = paste0(detected_n, "/", total_n)),
      nudge_x = 0.10,
      hjust = 0,
      size = nm_style$detection_prevalence_label,
      colour = "grey30"
    ) +

    geom_text(
      data =
        p_text,
      aes(x = "Fisher p", y = GeneLabel, label = p_label, fontface = p_face),
      hjust = 0.5,
      size = nm_style$detection_p_label,
      colour = "grey30"
    ) +

    # Use the same full scale in Female and Male panels so patchwork
    # can collect a single unified cellular-component legend.
        scale_colour_manual(
      values =
        bin_pal_dot[legend_bins],

      breaks =
        legend_bins,

      limits =
        legend_bins,

      drop = FALSE,

      name =
        "Cellular component"
    ) +

    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1, shape = 16, size = nm_style$detection_filled))) +

    scale_x_discrete(
      limits = c("Old Ctl", "Old+Ex", "Old+Rapa", "Fisher p"),
      position = "top",
      drop = FALSE,
      expand =
        expansion(add = c(0.15, 0.30))
    ) +

    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +

    labs(title = title_text, subtitle = subtitle_text, x = NULL, y = NULL) +

    theme_classic(base_size = 11.5) +

    theme(
      plot.title =
        element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),

      plot.subtitle =
        element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 9.5),

      axis.text.x.top =
        element_text(face = "bold", size = nm_style$axis_text),

      axis.text.y =
        element_text(size = 8.5),

      axis.line =
        element_blank(),

      axis.ticks =
        element_blank(),

      panel.grid =
        element_blank(),

      legend.position =
        "right",

      legend.box =
        "vertical",

      plot.margin =
        margin(5, 8, 5, 5)
    )
}
```

```{r run-sex-specific-detection-pattern-plots, fig.keep="none"}
count_detection_pattern_by_sex <- function(flag_col) {

  out <- detection_bysex %>%
    filter(.data[[flag_col]]) %>%
    count(Sex, name = "n") %>%
    tidyr::complete(Sex = factor(c("Female", "Male"), levels = c("Female", "Male")), fill = list(n = 0))

  c(Female = out$n[as.character(out$Sex) == "Female"], Male = out$n[as.character(out$Sex) == "Male"])
}

combine_detection_sex_panels <- function(p_female, p_male, overall_title, n_female, n_male) {

  # Keep approximately the same vertical spacing per protein row.
  # The smaller panel occupies proportionally less vertical space and is
  # top-aligned; a spacer fills the unused area beneath it.
  n_max <- max(c(n_female, n_male, 1))

  make_top_aligned_column <- function(p, n_rows) {

    data_units <- max(n_rows, 1)

    spacer_units <- max(n_max - data_units, 0)

    if (spacer_units == 0) {
      return(p)
    }

    p /
      patchwork::plot_spacer() +

      patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(data_units, spacer_units))
  }

  female_col <- make_top_aligned_column(p_female, n_female)

  male_col <- make_top_aligned_column(p_male, n_male)

  patchwork::wrap_plots(female_col, male_col, ncol = 2, guides = "collect") +

    patchwork::plot_annotation() &

    theme(legend.position = "right", legend.box = "vertical")
}

n_shared <- count_detection_pattern_by_sex("Shared_loss")

n_exspec <- count_detection_pattern_by_sex("Exercise_specific_loss")

n_rapaspec <- count_detection_pattern_by_sex("Rapamycin_specific_loss")

p_shared_sex <- combine_detection_sex_panels(
```

# Female-versus-Male overlap of mutually exclusive loss patterns

The overlap analysis now uses the same mutually exclusive pattern definitions as the figures above rather than the broader pairwise `Exercise_reduced` and `Rapamycin_reduced` flags.

```{r detection-pattern-sex-overlap}
make_pattern_overlap <- function(flag_col, pattern_label) {

  pattern_tbl <- detection_bysex %>%
    filter(.data[[flag_col]]) %>%
    transmute(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Sex = as.character(Sex))

  female_tbl <- pattern_tbl %>%
    filter(Sex == "Female") %>%
    transmute(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Female = TRUE)

  male_tbl <- pattern_tbl %>%
    filter(Sex == "Male") %>%
    transmute(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Male = TRUE)

  full_join(female_tbl, male_tbl, by = c("Protein.Group", "Gene1", "Bin")) %>%
    mutate(
      Female =
        replace_na(Female, FALSE),

      Male =
        replace_na(Male, FALSE),

      Pattern =
        pattern_label,

      Overlap = case_when(
        Female &
          Male ~
          "Both sexes",

        Female &
          !Male ~
          "Female only",

        !Female &
          Male ~
          "Male only",

        TRUE ~
          "Neither"
      )
    )
}

loss_overlap_all <- bind_rows(
  make_pattern_overlap("Shared_loss", "Shared loss"),

  make_pattern_overlap("Exercise_specific_loss", "Exercise-specific loss"),

  make_pattern_overlap("Rapamycin_specific_loss", "Rapamycin-specific loss")
)

loss_overlap_summary <- loss_overlap_all %>%
  filter(Overlap != "Neither") %>%
  count(Pattern, Overlap, name = "n") %>%
  tidyr::complete(
    Pattern = c("Shared loss", "Exercise-specific loss", "Rapamycin-specific loss"),

    Overlap = c("Both sexes", "Female only", "Male only"),

    fill = list(n = 0)
  )

write.csv(loss_overlap_all, file.path(split_detect_dir, "DetectPattern_SexOverlap.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(
  loss_overlap_summary,
  file.path(split_detect_dir, "DetectPattern_SexOverlap_summary.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(
  loss_overlap_summary,
  caption =
    "Female-versus-Male overlap of mutually exclusive detection-loss patterns"
)
```

# Cellular-component summary of sex-specific loss patterns

Counts and percentages are now summarized for the same three mutually exclusive loss patterns. The denominator is the number of proteins **robustly detected in Old Control (≥2 detections)** within each sex and cellular component.

```{r treatment-detection-component-summary}
sex_detection_cols <- c("Female" = "#CC79A7", "Male" = "#0072B2")

control_robust_by_component <- detection_bysex %>%
  filter(Bin %in% dot_bin_order, detected_n_Control >= min_detect_n) %>%
  count(Sex, Bin, name = "n_control_robust")

component_detection_summary <- detection_bysex %>%
  filter(Bin %in% dot_bin_order) %>%
  select(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Sex, Shared_loss, Exercise_specific_loss, Rapamycin_specific_loss) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Shared_loss, Exercise_specific_loss, Rapamycin_specific_loss),
    names_to =
      "Pattern",
    values_to =
      "Is_loss"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Pattern = dplyr::recode(
      Pattern,
      Shared_loss =
        "Shared loss",
      Exercise_specific_loss =
        "Exercise-specific loss",
      Rapamycin_specific_loss =
        "Rapamycin-specific loss"
    ),

    Pattern = factor(Pattern, levels = c("Shared loss", "Exercise-specific loss", "Rapamycin-specific loss")),

    Sex = factor(Sex, levels = c("Female", "Male"))
  ) %>%
  filter(Is_loss) %>%
  count(Sex, Bin, Pattern, name = "n_loss") %>%
  tidyr::complete(
    Sex = factor(c("Female", "Male"), levels = c("Female", "Male")),

    Bin =
      dot_bin_order,

    Pattern = factor(
      c("Shared loss", "Exercise-specific loss", "Rapamycin-specific loss"),
      levels = c("Shared loss", "Exercise-specific loss", "Rapamycin-specific loss")
    ),

    fill = list(n_loss = 0)
  ) %>%
  left_join(control_robust_by_component, by = c("Sex", "Bin")) %>%
  mutate(
    n_control_robust =
      replace_na(n_control_robust, 0L),

    prop_loss = if_else(n_control_robust > 0, n_loss / n_control_robust, NA_real_),

    Bin = factor(Bin, levels = rev(dot_bin_order))
  )

write.csv(
  component_detection_summary,
  file.path(split_detect_dir, "TreatmentReduced_ComponentSummary_bySex.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

p_component_reduced_count <- ggplot(component_detection_summary, aes(x = n_loss, y = Bin, fill = Sex)) +

  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.76), width = nm_style$detection_summary_bar) +

  geom_text(
    aes(label = n_loss),
    position =
      position_dodge(width = 0.76),
    hjust = -0.18,
    size = nm_style$detection_summary_text
  ) +

  facet_wrap(~ Pattern, nrow = 1) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = sex_detection_cols) +

  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +

  labs(title = "Detection-loss patterns by cellular component", x = "Number of proteins", y = NULL, fill = "Sex") +

  theme_classic(base_size = 11.5) +

  theme(
    plot.title =
      element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),

    strip.text =
      element_text(face = "bold", size = 9.5),

    legend.position =
      "top"
  )

p_component_reduced_prop <- ggplot(component_detection_summary, aes(x = prop_loss, y = Bin, fill = Sex)) +

  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.76), width = nm_style$detection_summary_bar, na.rm = TRUE) +

  geom_text(
    data =
      component_detection_summary %>%
      filter(!is.na(prop_loss)),
    aes(label = scales::percent(prop_loss, accuracy = 1)),
    position =

  ) +

  facet_wrap(~ Pattern, nrow = 1) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = sex_detection_cols) +

  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +

  labs(
    title =
      "Loss-pattern prevalence among Old-Control-detected proteins",

    x =
      "Pattern / robust Old-Control proteins",

    y = NULL,

    fill =
      "Sex"
  ) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 11.5) +

  theme(
    plot.title =

p_component_reduced_combined <-
  p_component_reduced_count +
  p_component_reduced_prop +

  patchwork::plot_layout(ncol = 1, guides = "collect") &

  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

# Female-versus-Male changes in detection prevalence

The mutually exclusive loss-pattern figures above address intervention specificity. The scatterplots below answer a different, pairwise question: **how much did detection prevalence change after each intervention versus Old Control within Female and Male mice?**

For each intervention, the x-axis is the change in detection prevalence within Female mice and the y-axis is the corresponding change within Male mice:

\[
\Delta prevalence =
Prevalence_{Treatment} -
Prevalence_{Control}
\]

The dotted `y = x` line indicates identical treatment-associated changes in Female and Male mice. Shape denotes whether either within-sex Fisher test reaches raw `p ≤ 0.05`.

```{r treatment-detection-female-male-data}
make_detection_sex_scatter_data <- function(treatment_name) {

  treatment_name <- match.arg(treatment_name, c("Exercise", "Rapamycin"))

  delta_col <- paste0("delta_prev_", treatment_name)

  p_col <- paste0("p_", treatment_name)

  fdr_col <- paste0("FDR_", treatment_name)

  testable_col <- paste0(treatment_name, "_testable")

  reduced_col <- paste0(treatment_name, "_reduced")

  specific_col <- if (treatment_name == "Exercise") {
    "Exercise_specific_loss"
  } else {
    "Rapamycin_specific_loss"
  }

  detection_bysex %>%

    # Keep both sexes until after pivoting so the x/y coordinates are retained
    # even when only one sex meets the specific-loss criterion.
    filter(Bin %in% dot_bin_order) %>%

    transmute(
      Protein.Group,
      Gene1,
      Bin,

      Sex =
        as.character(Sex),

      delta_prev =
        .data[[delta_col]],

      p_detect =
        .data[[p_col]],

      FDR_detect =
        .data[[fdr_col]],

      testable =
        .data[[testable_col]],

      reduced =
        .data[[reduced_col]],

      specific_loss =
        .data[[specific_col]]
    ) %>%

    pivot_wider(
      names_from =
        Sex,

      values_from = c(delta_prev, p_detect, FDR_detect, testable, reduced, specific_loss),

      names_glue =
        "{.value}_{Sex}"
    ) %>%

    mutate(
      testable_Female =
        tidyr::replace_na(testable_Female, FALSE),

      testable_Male =
        tidyr::replace_na(testable_Male, FALSE),

      specific_loss_Female =
        tidyr::replace_na(specific_loss_Female, FALSE),

      specific_loss_Male =
        tidyr::replace_na(specific_loss_Male, FALSE)
    ) %>%

    # Protein universe = union of proteins in the Female or Male
    # treatment-specific loss lists.
    filter(specific_loss_Female | specific_loss_Male) %>%

    mutate(
      Female_raw_sig =
        testable_Female &
        !is.na(p_detect_Female) &
          p_detect_Female <=
            0.05,

      Male_raw_sig =
        testable_Male &
        !is.na(p_detect_Male) &
          p_detect_Male <=
            0.05,

      Female_FDR_sig =
        testable_Female &
        !is.na(FDR_detect_Female) &
          FDR_detect_Female <=
            0.05,

      Male_FDR_sig =
        testable_Male &
        !is.na(FDR_detect_Male) &
          FDR_detect_Male <=
            0.05,

      Sex_difference_delta =
        delta_prev_Male -
          delta_prev_Female,

      Abs_sex_difference_delta =
        abs(Sex_difference_delta),

      Treatment =
        treatment_name
    )
}

# Shared-loss delta:
# protein universe = union of proteins meeting Shared_loss in Female or Male.
# The displayed shared delta is the mean prevalence after Exercise and
# Rapamycin minus Old-Control prevalence within each sex.
make_shared_detection_sex_scatter_data <- function() {

  detection_bysex %>%

    filter(Bin %in% dot_bin_order) %>%

    mutate(
      delta_prev_Shared =
        (prevalence_Exercise + prevalence_Rapamycin) /
          2 -
          prevalence_Control,

      Shared_testable =
        Exercise_testable |
          Rapamycin_testable,

      Shared_min_raw_p = case_when(
        is.na(p_Exercise) &
          is.na(p_Rapamycin) ~
          NA_real_,

        TRUE ~
          pmin(p_Exercise, p_Rapamycin, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),

      Shared_min_FDR = case_when(
        is.na(FDR_Exercise) &
          is.na(FDR_Rapamycin) ~
          NA_real_,

        TRUE ~
          pmin(FDR_Exercise, FDR_Rapamycin, na.rm = TRUE)
      )
    ) %>%

    transmute(
      Protein.Group,
      Gene1,
      Bin,

      Sex =
        as.character(Sex),

      delta_prev =
        delta_prev_Shared,

      p_detect =
        Shared_min_raw_p,

      FDR_detect =
        Shared_min_FDR,

      testable =
        Shared_testable,

      shared_loss =
        Shared_loss,

      p_Exercise,
      p_Rapamycin,
      FDR_Exercise,
      FDR_Rapamycin
    ) %>%

    pivot_wider(
      names_from =
        Sex,

      values_from = c(
        delta_prev,
        p_detect,
        FDR_detect,
        testable,
        shared_loss,
        p_Exercise,
        p_Rapamycin,
        FDR_Exercise,
        FDR_Rapamycin
      ),

      names_glue =
        "{.value}_{Sex}"
    ) %>%

    mutate(
      testable_Female =
        tidyr::replace_na(testable_Female, FALSE),

      testable_Male =
        tidyr::replace_na(testable_Male, FALSE),

      shared_loss_Female =
        tidyr::replace_na(shared_loss_Female, FALSE),

      shared_loss_Male =
        tidyr::replace_na(shared_loss_Male, FALSE)
    ) %>%

    filter(shared_loss_Female | shared_loss_Male) %>%

    mutate(
      Female_raw_sig =
        testable_Female &
        !is.na(p_detect_Female) &
          p_detect_Female <=
            0.05,

      Male_raw_sig =
        testable_Male &
        !is.na(p_detect_Male) &
          p_detect_Male <=
            0.05,

      Female_FDR_sig =
        testable_Female &
        !is.na(FDR_detect_Female) &
          FDR_detect_Female <=
            0.05,

      Male_FDR_sig =
        testable_Male &
        !is.na(FDR_detect_Male) &
          FDR_detect_Male <=
            0.05,

      Sex_difference_delta =
        delta_prev_Male -
          delta_prev_Female,

      Abs_sex_difference_delta =
        abs(Sex_difference_delta),

      Treatment =
        "Shared"
    )
}

detect_shared_female_male <- make_shared_detection_sex_scatter_data()

detect_ex_female_male <- make_detection_sex_scatter_data("Exercise")

detect_rapa_female_male <- make_detection_sex_scatter_data("Rapamycin")

write.csv(detect_ex_female_male, file.path(split_detect_dir, "DetectDelta_Ex_FvM.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(detect_rapa_female_male, file.path(split_detect_dir, "DetectDelta_Rapa_FvM.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r treatment-detection-female-male-scatter, fig.keep="none"}
make_detection_delta_scatter <- function(
  plot_df,
  title_text,
  subtitle_text,
  x_text,
  y_text,
  output_file,
  female_membership_col,
  male_membership_col
) {

  # ============================================================================
  # Base protein table
  # ============================================================================

  base_df <- plot_df %>%

    filter(is.finite(delta_prev_Female), is.finite(delta_prev_Male)) %>%

    mutate(
      Female_member =
        tidyr::replace_na(.data[[female_membership_col]], FALSE),

      Male_member =
        tidyr::replace_na(.data[[male_membership_col]], FALSE)
    ) %>%

    filter(Female_member | Male_member)

  # ============================================================================
  # Deterministic protein-level displacement for exact coordinate ties
  # ============================================================================

  jitter_radius <- 0.026

  jitter_tbl <- base_df %>%

    distinct(Protein.Group, Gene1, delta_prev_Female, delta_prev_Male) %>%

    arrange(delta_prev_Female, delta_prev_Male, Gene1, Protein.Group) %>%

    group_by(delta_prev_Female, delta_prev_Male) %>%

    mutate(
      overlap_n =
        n(),

      overlap_index =
        row_number(),

      jitter_angle =
        if_else(overlap_n > 1, 2 * pi * (overlap_index - 1) / overlap_n, 0),

      protein_jitter_x =
        if_else(overlap_n > 1, jitter_radius * cos(jitter_angle), 0),

      protein_jitter_y =
        if_else(overlap_n > 1, jitter_radius * sin(jitter_angle), 0)
    ) %>%

    ungroup() %>%

    select(Protein.Group, protein_jitter_x, protein_jitter_y, overlap_n)

  base_df <- base_df %>%
    left_join(jitter_tbl, by = "Protein.Group")

  # ============================================================================
  # Small sex-specific offset when the same protein occurs in both sex lists
  # ============================================================================

  sex_offset <- 0.012

  female_df <- base_df %>%

    filter(Female_member) %>%

    transmute(
      Protein.Group,
      Gene1,
      Bin,

      True_x =
        delta_prev_Female,

      True_y =
        delta_prev_Male,

      Plot_x =
        delta_prev_Female +
        protein_jitter_x -
        sex_offset,

      Plot_y =
        delta_prev_Male +
        protein_jitter_y +
        sex_offset,

      Sex =
        "Female",

      Significant =
        tidyr::replace_na(Female_raw_sig, FALSE)
    )

  male_df <- base_df %>%

    filter(Male_member) %>%

    transmute(
      Protein.Group,
      Gene1,
      Bin,

      True_x =
        delta_prev_Female,

      True_y =
        delta_prev_Male,

      Plot_x =
        delta_prev_Female +
        protein_jitter_x +
        sex_offset,

      Plot_y =
        delta_prev_Male +
        protein_jitter_y -
        sex_offset,

      Sex =
        "Male",

      Significant =
        tidyr::replace_na(Male_raw_sig, FALSE)
    )

  symbol_df <- bind_rows(female_df, male_df) %>%

    mutate(
      SymbolClass = case_when(

        Sex ==
          "Female" &
          !Significant ~
          "Female — NS",

        Sex ==
          "Female" &
          Significant ~
          "Female — p ≤ 0.05",

        Sex ==
          "Male" &
          !Significant ~
          "Male — NS",

        Sex ==
          "Male" &
          Significant ~
          "Male — p ≤ 0.05"
      ),

      SymbolClass = factor(
        SymbolClass,
        levels = c("Female — NS", "Female — p ≤ 0.05", "Male — NS", "Male — p ≤ 0.05")
      )
    )

  # ============================================================================
  # Significant-protein label anchors
  #
  # Label is anchored to the actual displayed significant symbol.
  # If significant in both sexes, use the midpoint of the displayed symbols.
  # ============================================================================

  label_df <- symbol_df %>%

    filter(Significant) %>%

    group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin) %>%

    summarise(label_x = mean(Plot_x, na.rm = TRUE), label_y = mean(Plot_y, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  # ============================================================================
  # Only cellular components represented in this figure
  # ============================================================================

  bins_present <- dot_bin_order[dot_bin_order %in% unique(as.character(symbol_df$Bin))]

  # ============================================================================
  # Plot
  # ============================================================================

  p <- ggplot() +

    geom_abline(
      slope = 1,
      intercept = 0,
      linetype = "dotted",
      colour = "grey35",
      linewidth = nm_style$scatter_identity_line
    ) +

    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey72", linewidth = nm_style$scatter_zero_line) +

    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey72", linewidth = nm_style$scatter_zero_line) +

    # Female — NS = open circle
    geom_point(
      data =
        symbol_df %>%
        filter(SymbolClass == "Female — NS"),

      aes(x = Plot_x, y = Plot_y, colour = Bin, shape = SymbolClass),

      size = nm_style$scatter_open,
      stroke = nm_style$scatter_stroke
    ) +

    # Female — significant = filled circle
    geom_point(
      data =
        symbol_df %>%
        filter(SymbolClass == "Female — p ≤ 0.05"),

      aes(x = Plot_x, y = Plot_y, colour = Bin, shape = SymbolClass),

      size = nm_style$scatter_filled,
      stroke = nm_style$scatter_stroke
    ) +

    # Male — NS = open triangle
    geom_point(
      data =
        symbol_df %>%
        filter(SymbolClass == "Male — NS"),

      aes(x = Plot_x, y = Plot_y, colour = Bin, shape = SymbolClass),

      size = nm_style$scatter_open,
      stroke = nm_style$scatter_stroke
    ) +

    # Male — significant = filled triangle
    geom_point(
      data =
        symbol_df %>%
        filter(SymbolClass == "Male — p ≤ 0.05"),

      aes(x = Plot_x, y = Plot_y, colour = Bin, shape = SymbolClass),

      size = nm_style$scatter_filled,
      stroke = nm_style$scatter_stroke
    ) +

    # Significant protein labels
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
      data =
        label_df,

      aes(x = label_x, y = label_y, label = Gene1, colour = Bin),

      size = nm_style$scatter_label,

      box.padding = 0.25,
      point.padding = 0.20,

      force = 2,

      min.segment.length = 0,

      segment.size = 0.14,
      segment.colour = "grey45",

      max.overlaps = Inf,

      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +

    scale_shape_manual(
      values = c("Female — NS" = 1, "Female — p ≤ 0.05" = 16, "Male — NS" = 2, "Male — p ≤ 0.05" = 17),

      limits = c("Female — NS", "Female — p ≤ 0.05", "Male — NS", "Male — p ≤ 0.05"),

      drop = FALSE,

      name =
        "Sex / Fisher test"
    ) +

    scale_colour_manual(
      values =
        bin_pal_dot[bins_present],

      breaks =
        bins_present,

      limits =
        bins_present,

      drop = FALSE,

      name =
        "Cellular component"
    ) +

    guides(
      shape = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(colour = "black", size = 3.7, alpha = 1)),

      colour = guide_legend(order = 2, override.aes = list(shape = 16, size = 3.5, alpha = 1))
    ) +

    coord_equal(xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1, 1), clip = "off") +

    labs(title = title_text, subtitle = subtitle_text, x = x_text, y = y_text) +

    theme_classic(base_size = 12.5) +

    theme(
      plot.title =
        element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),

      plot.subtitle =
        element_text(colour = "grey35", size = 10),

      legend.position =
        "right",

      legend.box =
        "vertical",

      plot.margin =
        margin(10, 15, 15, 10)
    )

  save_plot_png(p, output_file, width = 9.3, height = 7.5, dpi = 300)

  list(plot = p, symbols = symbol_df, labels = label_df, jitter = jitter_tbl)
}

# ==============================================================================
# Exercise
# ==============================================================================
```

## Alternative protein-wise delta plots

As an alternative to the Female-versus-Male delta scatters, the plots below place each protein on a separate row and show only the sex-specific symbols for which that protein actually meets the corresponding specific-loss criterion. These figures avoid x/y overplotting while retaining the same sex, significance, and cellular-component encodings.

```{r alternative-proteinwise-delta-plots, fig.keep="none"}
make_detection_proteinwise_delta <- function(treatment_name) {

  treatment_name <- match.arg(treatment_name, c("Exercise", "Rapamycin"))

  flag_col <- if (treatment_name == "Exercise") {
    "Exercise_specific_loss"
  } else {
    "Rapamycin_specific_loss"
  }

  delta_col <- paste0("delta_prev_", treatment_name)

  p_col <- paste0("p_", treatment_name)

  plot_df <- detection_bysex %>%

    filter(.data[[flag_col]], Bin %in% dot_bin_order) %>%

    transmute(
      Protein.Group,
      Gene1,
      Bin,

      Sex =
        as.character(Sex),

      Delta =
        .data[[delta_col]],

      Fisher_p =
        .data[[p_col]]
    ) %>%

    mutate(
      Significant =
        !is.na(Fisher_p) &
          Fisher_p <=
            0.05,

      SymbolClass = case_when(

        Sex ==
          "Female" &
          !Significant ~
          "Female — NS",

        Sex ==
          "Female" &
          Significant ~
          "Female — p ≤ 0.05",

        Sex ==
          "Male" &
          !Significant ~
          "Male — NS",

        Sex ==
          "Male" &
          Significant ~
          "Male — p ≤ 0.05"
      ),

      SymbolClass = factor(
        SymbolClass,
        levels = c("Female — NS", "Female — p ≤ 0.05", "Male — NS", "Male — p ≤ 0.05")
      )
    )

  protein_order <- plot_df %>%

    group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin) %>%

    summarise(Mean_delta = mean(Delta, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%

    arrange(factor(Bin, levels = dot_bin_order), Mean_delta) %>%

    mutate(ProteinLabel = make.unique(as.character(Gene1)))

  plot_df <- plot_df %>%

    left_join(protein_order %>% select(Protein.Group, ProteinLabel), by = "Protein.Group") %>%

    mutate(ProteinLabel = factor(ProteinLabel, levels = rev(protein_order$ProteinLabel)))

  bins_present <- dot_bin_order[dot_bin_order %in% unique(as.character(plot_df$Bin))]

  p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Delta, y = ProteinLabel, colour = Bin, shape = SymbolClass)) +

    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey65", linewidth = nm_style$scatter_zero_line) +

    geom_point(size = nm_style$proteinwise_point, stroke = nm_style$scatter_stroke, alpha = 0.95) +

    scale_shape_manual(
      values = c("Female — NS" = 1, "Female — p ≤ 0.05" = 16, "Male — NS" = 2, "Male — p ≤ 0.05" = 17),

      limits = c("Female — NS", "Female — p ≤ 0.05", "Male — NS", "Male — p ≤ 0.05"),

      drop = FALSE,

      name =
        "Sex / Fisher test"
    ) +

    scale_colour_manual(
      values =
        bin_pal_dot[bins_present],

      breaks =
        bins_present,

      limits =
        bins_present,

      drop = FALSE,

      name =
        "Cellular component"
    ) +

    guides(
      shape = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(colour = "black", size = 3.7, alpha = 1)),

      colour = guide_legend(order = 2, override.aes = list(shape = 16, size = 3.5, alpha = 1))
    ) +

    labs(
      title =
        paste0(treatment_name, "-specific loss of detection"),

      subtitle =
        paste0("Change in detection prevalence after ", treatment_name, " relative to Old Control"),

      x =
        paste0("Change in detection prevalence (", treatment_name, " vs Control)"),

      y = NULL
    ) +

    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +

    theme(
      plot.title =
        element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),

      plot.subtitle =
        element_text(colour = "grey35", size = 10),

      axis.text.y =
        element_text(size = 9.5),

      axis.line.y =
        element_blank(),

      axis.ticks.y =
        element_blank(),

      panel.grid.major.y =
        element_line(colour = "grey94", linewidth = 0.30),

      legend.position =
        "right",

      legend.box =
        "vertical"
    )

  list(plot = p, data = plot_df)
}
```

# Compact six-group detection-prevalence matrix

This display retains the actual Old-Control, Old+Exercise, and Old+Rapamycin detection prevalence in Female and Male mice for selected candidates.

Selection prioritizes proteins with raw within-sex Fisher `p ≤ 0.05` for either intervention, followed by proteins meeting a treatment-reduced criterion. The default maximum is 18 proteins.

```{r selected-six-group-detection-data}
max_detection_matrix_proteins <- 18

detection_candidate_wide <- detection_bysex %>%
  filter(Bin %in% dot_bin_order) %>%
  transmute(
    Protein.Group,
    Gene1,
    Bin,
    Sex =
      as.character(Sex),

    p_Exercise,
    FDR_Exercise,
    p_Rapamycin,
    FDR_Rapamycin,

    Exercise_reduced,
    Rapamycin_reduced,

    delta_prev_Exercise,
    delta_prev_Rapamycin
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from =
      Sex,

    values_from = c(
      p_Exercise,
      FDR_Exercise,
      p_Rapamycin,
      FDR_Rapamycin,
      Exercise_reduced,
      Rapamycin_reduced,
      delta_prev_Exercise,
      delta_prev_Rapamycin
    ),

    names_glue =
      "{.value}_{Sex}"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Any_raw_sig =
      (!is.na(p_Exercise_Female) & p_Exercise_Female <= 0.05) |
      (!is.na(p_Exercise_Male) & p_Exercise_Male <= 0.05) |
      (!is.na(p_Rapamycin_Female) & p_Rapamycin_Female <= 0.05) |
      (!is.na(p_Rapamycin_Male) & p_Rapamycin_Male <= 0.05),

    Any_reduced =
      replace_na(Exercise_reduced_Female, FALSE) |
      replace_na(Exercise_reduced_Male, FALSE) |
      replace_na(Rapamycin_reduced_Female, FALSE) |
      replace_na(Rapamycin_reduced_Male, FALSE),

    min_raw_p = pmin(p_Exercise_Female, p_Exercise_Male, p_Rapamycin_Female, p_Rapamycin_Male, na.rm = TRUE),

    max_abs_delta = pmax(
      abs(delta_prev_Exercise_Female),
      abs(delta_prev_Exercise_Male),
      abs(delta_prev_Rapamycin_Female),
      abs(delta_prev_Rapamycin_Male),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )

candidate_ranking <- detection_candidate_wide %>%
  filter(Any_raw_sig | Any_reduced) %>%
  arrange(desc(Any_raw_sig), min_raw_p, desc(max_abs_delta)) %>%
  slice_head(n = max_detection_matrix_proteins) %>%
  mutate(Selection_rank = row_number(), GeneLabel = make.unique(as.character(Gene1)))

write.csv(
  candidate_ranking,
  file.path(split_detect_dir, "Detection_SelectedCandidates_ranking.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

selected_detection_matrix <- long_assigned %>%
  mutate(Detected = Intensity > 0) %>%
  semi_join(candidate_ranking %>% select(Protein.Group), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
  group_by(Protein.Group, Gene1, Bin, Treatment, Sex) %>%
  summarise(
    detected_n =
      sum(Detected, na.rm = TRUE),

    total_n =
      n(),

    prevalence =
      detected_n /
        total_n,

    .groups =
      "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(candidate_ranking %>% select(Protein.Group, Selection_rank, GeneLabel), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
  mutate(
    Group = factor(paste(Treatment, Sex, sep = "_"), levels = group_levels_6),

    GeneLabel = factor(GeneLabel, levels = rev(candidate_ranking$GeneLabel))
  )

write.csv(
  selected_detection_matrix,
  file.path(split_detect_dir, "Detection_SelectedCandidates_6GroupMatrix.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# Absolute and centered abundance alternatives

These figures use the pooled Old-Control-ranked Top-10 protein set and the same six Treatment × Sex groups.

- **Absolute heatmap:** fill = `log10(mean intensity)` among positive detections.
- **Centered heatmap:** each protein's six-group mean `log10` abundance is subtracted from each group value.
- **Centered bubble plot:** color gives the signed centered value; point size gives its absolute magnitude.

The centered displays emphasize within-protein Treatment × Sex patterns. They should not be used to compare absolute abundance across different proteins.

```{r top10-treatment-sex-heatmap-data}
top10_heatmap_tbl <- pooled_control_top10_bysex %>%
  mutate(
    log10_intensity = if_else(!is.na(mean_intensity) & mean_intensity > 0, log10(mean_intensity), NA_real_)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Protein.Group) %>%
  mutate(
    protein_mean_log10 = if_else(any(is.finite(log10_intensity)), mean(log10_intensity, na.rm = TRUE), NA_real_),

    centered_log10 = if_else(
      is.finite(log10_intensity) &
        is.finite(protein_mean_log10),
      log10_intensity -
        protein_mean_log10,
      NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

write.csv(
  top10_heatmap_tbl,
  file.path(split_dot_dir, "Top10_PooledCtl_TreatSex_heatmap_values.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

absolute_limits <- range(top10_heatmap_tbl$log10_intensity, na.rm = TRUE)

center_abs_max <- max(abs(top10_heatmap_tbl$centered_log10), na.rm = TRUE)

if (!is.finite(center_abs_max) || center_abs_max == 0) {
  center_abs_max <- 1
}
```

## Absolute abundance heatmap

```{r absolute-treatment-sex-heatmap, fig.keep="none"}
absolute_heatmap_list <- list()

for (i in seq_along(dot_bin_order)) {

  bin_name <- dot_bin_order[i]
  bin_col  <- bin_pal_dot[[bin_name]]

  rank_tbl <- pooled_control_top10 %>%
    filter(Bin == bin_name) %>%
    arrange(Rank_Control) %>%
    mutate(GeneLabel = make.unique(as.character(Gene1)))

  plot_df <- top10_heatmap_tbl %>%
    filter(as.character(Bin) == bin_name) %>%
    left_join(rank_tbl %>% select(Protein.Group, GeneLabel), by = "Protein.Group") %>%
    mutate(GeneLabel = factor(GeneLabel, levels = rev(rank_tbl$GeneLabel)))

  if (nrow(plot_df) == 0) {
    next
  }

  p <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Group, y = GeneLabel, fill = log10_intensity)) +

    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = nm_style$heatmap_tile_line) +

    geom_vline(xintercept = 3.5, colour = "grey65", linewidth = nm_style$heatmap_divider) +

    geom_text(
      data =
        plot_df %>%
        filter(is.na(log10_intensity)),
      aes(label = "ND"),
      colour = "grey55",
      size = nm_style$heatmap_text
    ) +

    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      option = "C",
      limits =
        absolute_limits,
      oob =
        scales::squish,
      na.value =
        "grey95",
      name = expression(log[10]("mean intensity"))
    ) +

    scale_x_discrete(position = "top", labels = group_labels_6) +

    labs(title = bin_name, x = NULL, y = NULL) +

    theme_classic(base_size = 11) +

    theme(
      plot.title =
        element_text(face = "bold", size = nm_style$component_heading, colour = bin_col),

      axis.text.x =
        element_text(size = nm_style$top10_group_pt, face = "bold"),

      axis.text.y =
        element_text(size = nm_style$top10_protein_pt),

      axis.line =
        element_blank(),

      axis.ticks =
        element_blank(),

      panel.grid =
        element_blank(),

      legend.position =
        if (i == 1) {
          "right"
        } else {
          "none"
        }
    )

  absolute_heatmap_list[[bin_name]] <- p
}

absolute_heatmap_combined <-
  patchwork::wrap_plots(absolute_heatmap_list, ncol = 4) +

  patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") +

  patchwork::plot_annotation() &

  theme(legend.position = "right")

absolute_heatmap_png <- file.path(split_dot_dir, "Top10_PooledCtl_TrtSex_AbsolHM.png")

save_plot_png(absolute_heatmap_combined, absolute_heatmap_png, width = 14.8, height = 6.8, dpi = 300)
```

## Within-protein centered abundance heatmap

```{r centered-treatment-sex-heatmap, fig.keep="none"}
centered_heatmap_list <- list()

for (i in seq_along(dot_bin_order)) {

  bin_name <- dot_bin_order[i]
```


# Sex-resolved output guide

The newly added sex-resolved outputs are written under:

```text
Comp_OldTrt/
└── SexSplit/
    ├── Composition/
    ├── Stats/
    ├── Detection/
    └── TopProteins/
```

Key protein-level figures include:
